A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETNN research. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original QM9 prediction experiments, air-pollution regression and ablations, and synthetic 4-chain classification results.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and additionally reports counterexample classification, reproduced EMPSN results, and runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The ETNN message and position updates, geometric invariants, molecular/geospatial constructions, and implementation architecture remain unchanged. Appendix D explicitly formulates velocity handling already described as supported in v2 Section 3; this does not establish a changed underlying method.

E1.justification: v4 adds geometric counterexample scenarios involving 2-, 3-, and 4-body scalarization, beyond the retained 4-chain tests. It removes the QM9 R² prediction target from the property and results tables. The remaining molecular tasks and Bronx air-pollution coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v4 substantially expands QM9 comparisons with Equiformer, four TopNet variants, the authors' EMPSN reproduction, and EMPSN results reproduced by Verma et al. Original published EMPSN scores were already present in v2 Tables 8–9 and are retained; those are not a newly added comparator.

E3.justification: The new counterexample evaluation specifies single-layer models, four lifts, and invariant versus equivariant variants. v4 also introduces runtime/memory comparisons and specifies the Vietoris–Rips construction for its EMPSN reproduction. Existing QM9 training settings and air-pollution splitting and evaluation procedures remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds a substantial expressivity stress test across four lifts and invariant/equivariant variants, including failure on 4-body chiral counterexamples. Appendix G adds empirical runtime and memory analysis against EGNN and EMPSN. The original molecular ablations, air-pollution ablations, and 4-chain analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging air-pollution results over three seeds and 4-chain results over ten seeds. v4 adds no explicit repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedure; its additional averages do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds comparator, counterexample, runtime, and memory results and removes all QM9 R² results. Table 1 revises best-ETNN α from .066 to .062 and several other summary values; Appendix Table 12 changes the H summary from 11 to 12. Some revised summaries already appear among v2's configuration-level results, so they do not establish new performance gains. Air-pollution and 4-chain scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 adds the velocity-equivariance derivation and corrects factors and translation parentheses in the position-update proof. It also changes the augmented Hasse graph edge definition from an either-direction condition to directed neighborhood membership (v2 Equation 24 versus v4 Equation 27). The principal expressivity propositions and complexity derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add a prominent claim that ETNN matches or surpasses leading equivariant TDL models with substantially lower computational costs. They also claim success on scalarization counterexamples beyond the original k-hop analysis. These broaden the advertised empirical contributions while retaining the unifying-framework claim.

C2.justification: v4 removes v2's explicit discussion of poor R² prediction and the qualification that no fixed architecture wins across all targets. It adds efficiency explanations based on smaller molecular complexes and neighborhood processing, plus a claim of consistently outperforming TopNet. The new counterexample discussion identifies a chiral failure boundary, materially changing the paper's interpretation and qualifications.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies the five-layer air-pollution MLP, describes its EMPSN reproduction and sequential neighborhood processing, and provides resource measurements. Most hyperparameters, hardware specifications, feature-processing instructions, and architecture details already appear in v2. The repository and reproducibility-material access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds TopNets and its persistent-homology positioning. Appendix C.3 qualifies cellular-network novelty by acknowledging Kovač et al.; new references also support counterexamples, geometric learning, and pollution data. The broader positioning as a unifying equivariant framework remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 revises contribution and experiment paragraphs, adds a velocity appendix, and moves the reproducibility statement before the bibliography. Citations change to author–year format and headings are restyled, but most prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reformats the document and comparison displays: it adds counterexample, runtime, and memory tables, enlarges molecular comparison tables, removes the R² column, and redistributes figures and tables. Title, author, heading, and running-header layouts change. The eleven existing figure illustrations themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The reproduced EMPSN comparison, counterexample tests, resource measurements, and proof corrections improve evaluability. However, v4 removes the poorly performing R² target and its limitation without explanation. Its new 'almost half' runtime claim conflicts with Table 5: 193.16 versus 251.3 seconds per epoch implies approximately 23% less time. The added evidence and these material reporting problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
